title: WinAcc: Window-based Acceleration of Neural Networks Using Block Floating Point
problem: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) require high computational and energy efficiency, but floating-point accumulations between vectors create bottlenecks. State-of-the-art approaches using grouped summation based on exponent differences increase register complexity and limit energy benefits.
motivation: DNNs impose significant computational demands; optimizing both storage and computational overhead is critical. Current BFP (Block Floating Point) accumulators have high area overhead and limited energy efficiency gains.
method: Neural network data naturally follows a Laplace-like distribution—most values cluster around zero with few large outliers. WinAcc exploits this by using a narrow dynamic-range data format (a restricted range of representable numbers) instead of standard floating-point, since most values fall within this narrow window. This simpler representation uses only narrow shifters and narrow adders (simpler versions of floating-point hardware) for combining values, reducing both register complexity and energy consumption.
key_novelty: WinAcc's key insight is recognizing that neural network data follows a Laplace-like distribution (values concentrate around zero), which enables building accumulators with a narrow dynamic range instead of expensive floating-point units.
contributions: 33.95% energy reduction across seven representative DNNs
primary_theme: Low-cost BFP accumulator with Laplace-aware format
